changed.what: Applied three requests: the M1 load is 60 convergence parts (GATE-MARROW-01's completing part recorded by N13-19 with --part M1; GATE-MARROW-06's M1 part is the referee rows of N13-36), with due_counts and the known answers updated; NAB-24 added to deps and the decision sweep now runs before the review as the attached check decision-sweep (BET-12 alone comes after); N25bp4-01 added to deps (it records GATE-WS-03's M1 part). Unchanged, the review would have counted 59 parts against N40-04's 60 and could have run before the sweep and the GATE-WS-03 M1 part it reads. The acceptance line for KILL-TENFOLD-LEVER now asks for its one decision ADR (docs/adr/ADR-KILL-TENFOLD-LEVER-M1.md, holding the eight per-lever records of N39a-39) and the register row's entry with exit = "M1", in place of 'eight decision records', which an exit reviewer would have sought as eight ADRs (convention 10).

Removed the narration that prereg-section-missing and prereg-rule-paraphrased were still requested of N39-REF; they are its rows (exit 3, raised_by BD-314) and the bead now says so (convention 13). An implementer would otherwise have waited for, or added, rows that already exist.

The M7 exit review had no Bets section although N40-31 makes BET-13 and BET-14 due at M7 and the other exit reviews (BD-378, BD-427, BD-442) carry one. Added the acceptance clause and the unit test bets_due_m7 (the due set is exactly {BET-13, BET-14}; an open bet makes the exit not-ready; a stratum measured between 3 and 10 neither holds nor falsifies BET-13). Without it M7 could exit with both bets undecided.

The strict reading named no reason ids or exit codes. It now names the N39-REF rows it raises (record-unknown-field, record-missing-field, record-duplicate-key, record-noncanonical-number, record-unknown-schema at exit 3; record-hash-mismatch and store-overwrite at exit 9) with N39-REF's refusal shape, and the record check and unit tests assert them. Otherwise the implementer would invent ids that N39-REF's two-way consistency test then rejects.

capabilities_resolve accepted only IA-nn ids, but the audit (N39b-08 step 2) fills a comparator row's capabilities with IA, DA and NF ids, and N00-14 writes the DA and NF records into the same incumbent_audit.toml. The test and the Scope now resolve ids of any record of that file; as written, every audited row would have been a load error.

Wrote the planted input false_certificate (TF-CX-11, GATE-TENFOLD-03) under its plant name in fixtures/tenfold/controls/, with what makes it caught and who disqualifies and decides (N39b-01, N39b-03); registered its three answer kinds in N39a-09's decision table that frob-tenfold adjudicate runs; added N39a-08 to deps, since step 5(c) samples in the adjudicating simulator whose adapter N39a-08 builds. Without these the registry entry had no fixture, the e2e's adjudicate call had no definition, and the bead could start before its simulator existed.

The e2e scripts of N39a-06, N39a-07 and this bead call frob-tenfold submit and frob-tenfold adjudicate, but no bead defined adjudicate. This bead now owns both subcommands (submit: commit and spend; adjudicate: draw, decide through a table keyed by answer kind, sign the receipt; adjudicator role only, N39a-02) and its script uses them. Unchanged, the scripts called a subcommand that nothing builds (convention 8).

States that its battery procedure is registered for qualified-design and counterexample-and-repair in N39a-09's decision table, which frob-tenfold adjudicate (called by its e2e script) runs. Without it nothing connects the battery to the subcommand the script calls.

N40-14 names this bead the recorder of GATE-TENFOLD-05, but the script wrote 'the gate record' and nothing entered the register part. It now commits the per-stratum records and the run receipt under receipts/gates/ and records the part with record_gate --gate GATE-TENFOLD-05 --part M3|M7 from a fresh session (convention 9); control (d) is named as TF-CX-15 with its plant judge_in_tuning_logs (N39a-08). Unchanged, may_open would find no -05 pass part, or a script would write the register itself.

N40-14 names this bead the recorder of GATE-TENFOLD-04, but nothing entered the register part. The record and the receipt of the control run are now committed under receipts/gates/, and the part is recorded with record_gate --gate GATE-TENFOLD-04 --part M3|M7 from the pre-open run, by a session that implemented none of the mechanisms (convention 9). Otherwise the pre-opening conjunction would find no -04 part.

Applied the request: the stratum record now has development_deadline_s (14,400 s by default, published with the class description, carried by development cards) beside deadline_s (the stratum's H, null until N39b-30 decides it, carried by sealed cards), and check 6 holds only sealed cards to deadline_s; unit test two_deadlines added. The e2e now runs the grid check as a rehearsal tournament as well, since check 3 refuses an empty cell only at a tournament. Before, every development card failed check 6 or N39a-05's check 4, and the script's empty-cell refusal could never occur on a partial-gate rehearsal.

Card check 4 now names the two stratum-record fields it compares against (deadline_s for sealed cards, development_deadline_s for development cards, N39a-12). Before, it pointed at a 'provisional deadline of the class description' that no record held.

Its own e2e and BD-314's call frob-tenfold seal step, which no bead defined. Added the command forms (seal step <n> --kind --payload [--arm], --complete, the open operation as seal step 6 --kind open, seal verify) with their exit codes, and named the refusals for an unregistered entry kind (seal-kind-unregistered, requested of N39-REF) and a role the kind does not allow (role-not-permitted); unit test kind_and_role_registry added. Otherwise the scripts called a nonexistent subcommand and the acceptance criterion's refusal of an unregistered kind had no reason id.
Its e2e and N39a-41 call frob-tenfold-score warm, which no bead defined; the bead now owns that subcommand (frob-tenfold-score warm <cell> [--json], exit 3 on refusal) (convention 8).

ledger check fails a ledger without a resolvable freeze manifest, yet the M0 and M1 baseline ledgers (BD-040, BD-143) are written before any freeze manifest exists (N39a-18, M3). A baseline ledger's freeze field now holds the content address of the frozen comparator-registry row (BD-039's registry, frozen by N36-25), which the check resolves; baseline_single_phase tests both cases. Otherwise every baseline ledger would fail its own check with ledger-disclosure-missing.

Its e2e, N39a-28 and N39a-41 call frob-tenfold-score cell, which no bead defined; the bead now owns the subcommand (frob-tenfold-score cell <cell> [--json], exit 3 with the first validation refusal) (convention 8).

Gave the bead its own e2e script, scripts/e2e/tenfold_bootstrap.sh (convention 11): the exact TF-26 reference values (recomputed here: p0 = 9,569/20,000, k_L = 398, k_U = 9,380, L = 612/469, U = 126/17), thread and build-mode identity, the degenerate case and a cross-platform digest; STD-E2E added to deps. Defined the subcommand frob-tenfold-score bootstrap <cell> [--seed] that N39a-41 calls. Before, the bead had no script, and the rehearsal's 'covered by' line called cell, not the bootstrap.

Gave the bead its own e2e script, scripts/e2e/tenfold_noninferiority.sh (convention 11; the table 59/93/124/153, the bounds and BinCDF(3; 60) = 0.647 recomputed), STD-E2E added to deps, and the subcommand frob-tenfold-score noninferiority <cell> defined beside --table. Built the mutation bootstrap_zero_counts that N39-CX assigns it (TF-CX-08), which zero_count_bound catches. Before, the registry entry had no plant and the bead had no script.

The combiner's refusal of a monitor stop at a tournament gate had no reason id; it is now monitor-stop-disarmed (exit 3; requested of N39-REF), and the e2e asserts it. Otherwise the implementer would invent an id that N39-REF's two-way consistency test rejects.

Wrote the planted input four_family_cell (TF-CX-07, gates GATE-TENFOLD-03 and -04) under its plant name in fixtures/tenfold/controls/, with the condition that catches it (condition iii failed, ten-fold unreachable, naming refused with cell-not-reachable) and who decides (N39a-34); N39a-40's control runner reads it. Before, N39a-40 cited a fixture that no bead wrote.

The TF-CX-26 paragraph assigned the refusal of an operator's stop request to N39b-13. It now names N39bp3-01 (frob-tenfold tournament stop-cell refused with tenfold.interim-stop-refused, exit 3), as N39-CX does, and keeps the fixture and the monitor side here; N39bp3-01 added to related. Otherwise an implementer would look for the refusal in the wrong bead.

Gave the report record its own e2e script, scripts/e2e/tenfold_report_record.sh (convention 11), built on its own dependencies through a new subcommand frob-tenfold report check [--render], because report build is N39b-14's and comes later. The script and two new unit tests (self_adjudicated_labelled, cost_claim_none) make the assertions this bead now solely owns: a self-adjudicated report carries the label and omits 'independently accepted' and 'ten-fold', and every report prints cost_claim: none. Rule 5's refusal is named report-locked-wording (requested of N39-REF, with the existing but unregistered report-contract-violation); STD-E2E added to deps. Before, those two assertions were made nowhere, and the 'covered by' script called a command this bead cannot reach.

The register entry now carries exit = "M1" as the first entry of the row's decision array (N40-03, N39b-10); the narration that a per-class field was 'requested of N00-09' is replaced by N00-09's actual field: a package struck for some classes is re-registered with those classes removed from classes (check g) (convention 13). Not applied: the request's 'fired only when a lever is struck_overall'. The bead's 'fired when any (lever, class) is struck' matches the trigger, the per-class fallback and N39b-10's M2 entry, and the request's form would record not-fired while a fallback is in force. The 'a new ADR at the M2 re-read' wording was already in place.

Step 11 runs frob-tenfold report build, which N39b-14 builds, but the bead did not depend on N39b-14 (both M3, no cycle). Added the dependency and named it at the step. Otherwise an agent could start the rehearsal and be unable to finish its report step.
Attributed frob-tenfold report build to N39a-36; N39a-36 says the command is N39b-14's (already a dependency). Corrected, so the implementer looks in the right bead.

requests.what: Add the harness reason seal-kind-unregistered: an entry offered to the sealing ledger whose kind is not in the ledger's kind registry (repair: register the kind with its payload schema and roles in the bead that writes it; exit 3; maps_to none; raised_by N39a-15; producing test N39a-15's seal::kind_and_role_registry).

Add the harness reason monitor-stop-disarmed: a futility-monitor stop offered to the cell outcome combiner for a cell of a gate of type tournament, where the stop is disarmed (repair: none, the cell runs to n; exit 3; maps_to none; raised_by N39a-32; producing test N39a-32's monitor_stop_combiner).

Add the harness reasons report-contract-violation (a report record failing the metric contract's check_report, listing the violations by letter; exit 3; raised_by N39a-36; producing test contract_violation_refuses_build; already used by N39a-36's rule 7 but not a row) and report-locked-wording (a locked phrase in the rendering of a self-adjudicated report, or 'ten-fold' on a cell whose verdict is not ten-fold; exit 3; raised_by N39a-36; producing test self_adjudicated_labelled).

Name the field: the 'provisional development deadline of the stratum's class description (4 h by default)' that development cards carry is the stratum record's development_deadline_s (N39a-12, 14,400 s by default); deadline_s there is the stratum's H, null until N39b-30 decides it.

Name the field: the provisional deadline used before this decision (14,400 s) is the stratum record's development_deadline_s (N39a-12); the deadline this decision sets is written to the stratum record's deadline_s.

notes: Unchanged after full review: BD-433, N39a-02, N39a-04, N39a-08, N39a-13, N39a-18, N39a-20, N39a-29, N39a-31, N39a-37, N39a-38, N39ax-03. Numbers recomputed with own scripts (bootstrap TF-26, guard tails and Holm steps, non-inferiority attainability 59/93/124/153 and BinCDF(3;60)=0.647, warm card, six-family card, ceilings, monitor E values, battery sizes). N39a-01: the audit's proposed split of N39-REF's harness-reason table (so that N39-REF no longer depends on N39a-01) was declined: N39-REF's unit tests run in N39a-01's test target (--test tenfold), its exit_codes test and e2e tenfold_refusals.sh provoke reasons through N39a-01's binaries, and its two-way consistency test reads harness source, so removing the edge would let N39-REF start and not finish; N39a-01 instead states the ids and exits it raises, which N39-REF binds. Dependencies added: N39a-07 -> N39a-08, N39a-41 -> N39b-14, STD-E2E to N39a-28, N39a-30 and N39a-36 (BD-147's NAB-24 and N25bp4-01 by request); graph_check reports no cycle. All 37 files parse (front matter, one-line JSON lists, seven sections).
